# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

```plantuml
class AutoPruneStrategy {
    addNodeAndUpdateBranch(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>) : void
    addNodeToTree(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>, currentNodeRef : node) : void
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode
    isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(queue : Deque) : void
}
class BaseNode {
    content : String
    levelSeq : List<int>
    levelText : String
    title : String
    concatNode(node : BaseNode) : void
}
class ChainNode {
    patternPriority : int
}
class ChainParser {
    patterns : List<LevelPattern>
    createChainNode(levelSeq : List<int>, title : String, content : String, levelText : String, patternPriority : int) : ChainNode
    detectLevel(line : String) : ChainNode
    parseToChain(text : String) : List<ChainNode>
}

    description : String
    failOnConvert : boolean
    fixedLevelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>

    minLevel : int
    numberType : NumberType
    regexText : String
    separator : String

    getRegex() : Pattern
}

}

    numberType : NumberType
    prefixRegex : String
    separator : String
    suffixRegex : String

    copySelf() : PatternBuilder
    modify(newPrefixRegex : String, newMinLevel : int) : PatternBuilder
    validate() : void
}
class StrictStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode

}

    strategy : TreeBuildingStrategy

}
abstract class TreeBuildingStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    getLastLevel(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : int
    getPrefix(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : List<EIntegerObject>
    isImmNext(frontSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, backSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
    isRoot(node : BaseNode) : boolean
}
class TreeExporter {
    escapeJson(s : String) : String
    exportChain(chain : List<ChainNode>) : String
    exportToJson(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportToJsonFile(tree : TreeNode, filePath : Path) : void
    exportTree(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportTreeInternal(node : TreeNode, prefix : String, isLast : boolean, isRoot : boolean) : String
    nodeToDict(node : TreeNode) : EMap
    toJson(obj : EJavaObject, indent : int) : String
}
class TreeNode {
    children : List<TreeNode>
    parent : TreeNode
    addChild(child : TreeNode) : void
    getFullContent() : String
    mergeAllChildren() : void
}
enum NumberType {
    ARABIC
    ROMAN
    CHINESE
    LETTER
    CIRCLED
}

LevelPattern --> ParserHelper : helper

TreeNode --|> BaseNode

TreeNode --> TreeNode : parent  'opposite: children
```

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
ChainParser::parseToChain
Summary:
Parses structured text into an ordered list of heading and content ChainNodes
and always returns a synthetic ROOT section.
Algorithm:
1. Split text into lines using newline and recognize carriage returns as line
   boundaries.
2. Initialize the result with a ChainNode titled "ROOT" and an empty level
   sequence.
3. Maintain a current content string, initially empty.
4. For each line in order:
   a. Call detectLevel.
   b. If it returns a heading node, append the accumulated ordinary text to
     the new heading as its initial content, append the node, and reset the
     accumulation.
   c. Otherwise, if the line is empty, append a newline to content so an
     empty line is still represented in the section text.
   d. Otherwise, append a newline between noncontiguous ordinary lines and
     then append the current line.
5. Append any remaining ordinary text to the last chain node's content.
6. Return the list containing ROOT first.
Related Features:
Pattern priority, first valid match, ordinary-text preservation, and synthetic
ROOT fallback.
Related Classes:
ChainParser, ChainNode, LevelPattern, ParserHelper
Input:
text is structured plain text. It may be null, empty, contain only
whitespace, or include mixed headings and content separated by \n or \r.
Each line's encoding is passed to detectLevel.
Output:
A non-null List<ChainNode>. The first node is titled "ROOT" with an empty
level sequence; later nodes preserve source order and have content.
Pre-condition:
patterns and ParserHelper are configured, and text is supplied in a Java
String whose characters are valid for the configured regexes.
Post-condition:
All source content is assigned to a section, headings retain source order,
only valid numeric patterns produce level sequences, and the result is never
empty.

ChainParser::createChainNode
Summary:
Constructs a ChainNode containing parsed heading metadata and initial content.
Algorithm:
1. Create a ChainNode.
2. Assign levelSeq, title, content, levelText, and patternPriority.
3. Preserve explicit null values where supplied; otherwise initialize
   string fields to empty strings when an empty representation is required by
   the parser.
4. Return the ChainNode.
Related Features:
ChainNode inherits BaseNode fields; patternPriority records the matching
pattern's priority.
Related Classes:
ChainNode, BaseNode, EIntegerObject
Input:
levelSeq is a list of integer-compatible EIntegerObject values.
title is the heading title text, excluding structural numbering.
content is the section's initial body text.
levelText is the original matched level indicator text.
patternPriority is an integer, where a lower ordinal indicates a pattern
tried earlier.
Output:
A newly allocated ChainNode containing all supplied values.
Pre-condition:
All parameters are supplied by an internal parser stage and are compatible
with their declared types.
Post-condition:
The returned ChainNode contains the supplied fields and is ready for
parseToChain or tree construction.

ChainParser::detectLevel
Summary:
Finds the first valid heading pattern matching a line and creates a ChainNode
for the matched heading.
Algorithm:
1. If line is null, return null.
2. Iterate patterns in their configured priority order.
3. For each pattern, obtain its compiled regex through getRegex and attempt
   a match against line.
4. Extract the matched numbering and title portions.
5. Convert the matched numbering through LevelPattern.convertMatchedText.
6. If conversion fails or produces no level sequence, continue to the next
   pattern.
7. If multiple patterns match, retain the first pattern in the ordered list
   and call createChainNode with that pattern's priority.
8. If no pattern converts successfully, return null.
Related Features:
ordered LevelPattern list, regex matching, number conversion, fixed level
sequence, level bounds, and first-match precedence.
Related Classes:
LevelPattern, ParserHelper, ChainNode, NumberType, EIntegerObject
Input:
line is a single non-null source-text line. The parser recognizes ordered
indicators, such as Arabic or Roman numbers, Chinese numerals, alphabetic
letters, and circled numbers, followed by a heading title.
Output:
A ChainNode for the first valid pattern, or null when line is empty,
unmatched, or has invalid numeric text.
Pre-condition:
patterns is non-null, contains valid patterns in priority order, and any
external ParserHelper is configured for the selected NumberType.
Post-condition:
The original line is not modified. On success, levelText contains matched
indicator text, title is the remaining heading text, and patternPriority
identifies the first valid pattern.

7. If multiple patterns match, retain the first pattern in the ordered list
   and call createChainNode with that pattern's priority.
8. If no pattern converts successfully, return null.
Related Features:
ordered LevelPattern list, regex matching, number conversion, fixed level
sequence, level bounds, and first-match precedence.
Related Classes:
LevelPattern, ParserHelper, ChainNode, NumberType, EIntegerObject
Input:
line is a single non-null source-text line. The parser recognizes ordered
indicators, such as Arabic or Roman numbers, Chinese numerals, alphabetic
letters, and circled numbers, followed by a heading title.
Output:
A ChainNode for the first valid pattern, or null when line is empty,
unmatched, or has invalid numeric text.
Pre-condition:
patterns is non-null, contains valid patterns in priority order, and any
external ParserHelper is configured for the selected NumberType.
Post-condition:
The original line is not modified. On success, levelText contains matched
indicator text, title is the remaining heading text, and patternPriority
identifies the first valid pattern.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
TreeNode::addChild
Summary:
Establishes a bidirectional parent-child relationship by appending a child.
Algorithm:
1. If child is null, perform no mutation.
2. If child.parent is not this, call child.setParent(this) or assign
   child.parent directly.
3. Append child to this.children if it is not already present.
4. If a cycle would be created, such as adding an ancestor below its
   descendant, reject the operation.
Related Features:
TreeNode.children and TreeNode.parent bidirectional links.
Related Classes:
TreeNode
Input:
child is a TreeNode, which may be null.
Output:
No return value.
Pre-condition:
Both nodes are non-null and neither relationship already creates a cycle.
Post-condition:
child appears in this.children exactly once, child.parent is this, and the
relationship does not introduce a cycle.

TreeNode::mergeAllChildren
Summary:
Flattens the receiver's immediate children by moving each child's full content
into the receiver's direct content in traversal order.
Algorithm:
1. Iterate each child in stored order.
2. Call child.getFullContent to obtain its content and all descendant content.
3. Call this.concatNode on a content-only BaseNode value.
4. Remove all children from the receiver after their content has been
   collected.
5. Return without changing the detached children's own stored content.
Related Features:
TreeNode.children, BaseNode.concatNode, TreeNode.getFullContent, and
separator-free concatenation.
Related Classes:
TreeNode, BaseNode
Input:
No explicit parameters. The receiver may have zero or more children.
Output:
No return value.
Pre-condition:
The receiver is non-null, its content is writable, and child parent links
point to the receiver.
Post-condition:
The receiver's direct content contains its prior content and all descendant
content in traversal order, and the receiver has no children. Parent links
of detached children are cleared.

TreeNode::getFullContent
Summary:
Returns this node's direct content followed by all descendant content in
traversal order.
Algorithm:
1. Start with this.content.
2. Traverse children in stored order using depth-first traversal.
3. Append each descendant's content directly, without injecting whitespace,
   line breaks, or other separators.
4. If this.content is null, treat it as empty.
5. Return the concatenated string.
Related Features:
TreeNode.content, TreeNode.children, child order, and recursive aggregation.
Related Classes:
TreeNode, BaseNode
Input:
No explicit parameters. The receiver supplies direct and descendant content.
Output:
A string containing receiver content followed by descendant content in
traversal order.
Pre-condition:
The receiver is non-null and child links are cycle-free and consistent.
Post-condition:
No node content or relationship is modified.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
PatternBuilder::copySelf
Summary:
Creates a separate PatternBuilder with the same configuration as this
builder.
Algorithm:
1. Allocate a new PatternBuilder.
2. Copy maxLevel, minLevel, numberType, prefixRegex, separator, and
   suffixRegex.
3. Return the independent copy.
Related Features:
All mutable configuration properties in PatternBuilder.
Related Classes:
PatternBuilder
Input:
No explicit parameters; this object supplies the source configuration.
Output:
A new PatternBuilder with equivalent field values.
Pre-condition:
The current builder's fields are readable. Validation is not automatically
required merely to copy a configuration.
Post-condition:
Modifying either builder does not change the other builder.

PatternBuilder::validate
Summary:
Validates that a pattern builder's configuration is complete and internally
consistent.
Algorithm:
1. If minLevel is negative, reject the configuration.
2. If maxLevel is less than minLevel, reject it.
3. If numberType, prefixRegex, or separator is null, reject it.
4. If prefixRegex is not a valid regular-expression fragment, reject it.
5. If the assembled pattern would be syntactically invalid, reject it.
6. If all checks pass, return without error.
Related Features:
minLevel, maxLevel, numberType, prefixRegex, separator, and suffixRegex.
Related Classes:
PatternBuilder, NumberType
Input:
No explicit parameters. Validation reads the builder configuration.
Output:
No return value. Invalid configuration is reported by throwing an
IllegalArgumentException with a field-specific message.
Pre-condition:
The object has been populated with candidate pattern settings.
Post-condition:
A successfully returned builder is valid for LevelPattern construction. An
exception leaves no fields altered.

PatternBuilder::modify
Summary:
Returns a modified copy of the builder with a new prefix regex and minimum
level while preserving the remaining configuration.
Algorithm:
1. Invoke copySelf.
2. Assign newPrefixRegex to the copy's prefixRegex.
3. Assign newMinLevel to the copy's minLevel.
4. Return the modified copy.
Related Features:
copySelf, prefixRegex, and minLevel.
Related Classes:
PatternBuilder
Input:
newPrefixRegex is a non-null regular-expression fragment used before the
number.
newMinLevel is an integer structural lower bound and must be non-negative.
Output:
A new PatternBuilder with the requested prefix and minimum level.
Pre-condition:
newPrefixRegex is syntactically valid, and newMinLevel is not greater than
maxLevel.
Post-condition:
The original builder is unchanged. All other copied fields remain equal to
their source values.

```plantuml
    isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(queue : Deque) : void
}
```

# Operation Specifications
AutoPruneStrategy::buildTree
Summary:
Builds an outline tree from a list of chain nodes while tolerating irregular
level jumps and preserving valid siblings in arrival order.
Algorithm:
1. If the chain is null or empty, create and return a TreeNode titled "ROOT".
2. Create the ROOT TreeNode with an empty level sequence.
3. Set currentBranch to [ROOT] and currentNodeRef to ROOT.
4. For each node in chain:
   a. If the node is the immediate next node of currentNodeRef according to
      TreeBuildingStrategy.isImmNext, attach it to the appropriate prefix
      ancestor and update currentBranch.
   b. Otherwise, add the node to a FIFO pending queue rather than attaching
      it immediately.
   c. If the queue size is at least three, inspect all currently queued
      nodes. If every queued node forms an immediate sibling sequence, attach
      them in order. Otherwise merge the oldest queued node into the current
      node's content and remove it from the queue.
5. Merge every remaining pending node into the content of the current node,
  in arrival order, after all input has been processed.
6. Return ROOT.
Related Features:
ROOT title, empty ROOT level sequence, pending queue, current branch, and
preservation of child order.
Related Classes:
ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy, BaseNode
Input:
chain is a list of ChainNodes in source order. Each list element is non-null.
A null list is treated as empty.
Output:
A TreeNode titled "ROOT". Its descendants represent attached headings, while
unattachable pending content is concatenated into the current section.
Pre-condition:
ChainNode fields required by the strategy, particularly levelSeq, are
non-null. The strategy does not require all sequences to form a strict chain.
Post-condition:
The returned tree has a nonempty ROOT node; every attached child is reachable
from it, all parent-child links are consistent, children are ordered, and all
pending nodes have been merged into content without synthetic separators.

AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeAndUpdateBranch
Summary:
Attaches a chain node to the tree and updates currentBranch so it continues to
represent the latest valid root-to-node path.
Algorithm:
1. Locate the nearest existing node in currentBranch whose level sequence is
   a prefix of the new node's level sequence.
2. Convert the chain node to a TreeNode and attach it to that ancestor.
3. Remove descendants from currentBranch that are incompatible with the new
   path and append the new TreeNode.
4. If no valid prefix ancestor exists, retain the ROOT TreeNode as the only
   valid ancestor, because the first structural level must be empty.
Related Features:
TreeNode.addChild; currentBranch; inherited TreeBuildingStrategy.isRoot,
getPrefix, and isImmNext.
Related Classes:
ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input:
node is a non-null ChainNode containing title, level sequence, level text,
and content. levelSeq must be non-null, and a non-root sequence must not be
empty.
currentBranch is a mutable list of TreeNodes whose order is root-to-current.
Output:
No return value. The method updates currentBranch and the parent/child
relationship in the tree.
Pre-condition:
node is structurally valid, and currentBranch is non-null and contains a
root node followed by a valid chain of descendants.
Post-condition:
The new TreeNode is attached to the nearest valid prefix ancestor, its parent
points to that ancestor, currentBranch is the root-to-new-node path, and all
children remain uniquely reachable from the root.

AutoPruneStrategy::isAllNotImmNodesSiblings
Summary:
Determines whether all nodes currently held in the pending queue are
consecutive immediate siblings, and consumes the successful queue as part of
the strategy's update.
Algorithm:
1. If the queue contains fewer than three nodes, return without mutation.
2. Compare each node with the next node using the inherited immediate-next
   relationship, with all nodes at the same structural level.
3. If every adjacent pair is an immediate sibling sequence, remove those
   nodes from the queue so addNodeAndUpdateBranch can attach them in order.
4. Otherwise leave the queue unchanged for the caller to merge the oldest
   pending node.
Related Features:
FIFO pending queue; inherited TreeBuildingStrategy.isImmNext.
Related Classes:
ChainNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input:
queue is a non-null Deque containing at least three ChainNodes in arrival
order.
Output:
No explicit value is produced. The queue is emptied only when all pending
nodes are immediate siblings. The caller uses the mutation as the positive
result and invokes its merge rule otherwise.
Pre-condition:
The queue contains non-null ChainNodes ordered by arrival.
Post-condition:
When successful, the tested nodes are removed and remain available in their
original order. Otherwise the queue is unchanged.

AutoPruneStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary:
Creates a TreeNode view of a ChainNode for use by the auto-prune strategy.
Algorithm:
1. Allocate a TreeNode.
2. Copy the ChainNode title, level sequence, level text, and content.
3. Set the TreeNode parent to null and its child collection to an empty list.
4. Return the TreeNode.
Related Features:
TreeNode.parent, TreeNode.children, BaseNode data fields.
Related Classes:
ChainNode, TreeNode, BaseNode
Input:
chainnode is a non-null ChainNode with initialized document fields.
Output:
A detached TreeNode whose data fields correspond to chainnode.
Pre-condition:
chainnode is not null. A level sequence is accepted because structural repair
is performed by the auto-prune strategy.
Post-condition:
The returned TreeNode is detached, has an empty child list, and contains the
same title, level sequence, level text, and content as chainnode.

AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeToTree
Summary:
Adds a new tree node below the current node and makes currentNodeRef identify
that new node for subsequent processing.
Algorithm:
1. Create a TreeNode from the supplied ChainNode.
2. If the current node is a root node, the new node becomes its child;
   otherwise attach the new node below the nearest valid ancestor identified
   from the structural context.
3. Append the new node to currentBranch.
4. Replace currentNodeRef with the newly attached TreeNode.
Related Features:
TreeNode.parent, TreeNode.children, currentNodeRef, currentBranch.
Related Classes:
ChainNode, TreeNode, BaseNode
Input:
node is the ChainNode to attach.
currentBranch is a mutable root-to-current list of TreeNodes.
currentNodeRef is a mutable node reference; it is dereferenced and updated
during the operation.
Output:
No return value. The caller's node reference is updated to the new TreeNode.
Pre-condition:
currentBranch and the reference to currentNodeRef are non-null, and the
supplied node's level sequence is compatible with the current tree.
Post-condition:
A new TreeNode exists as the current node, has a valid parent, and represents
the same title, level sequence, level text, and content as node.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

```text
If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.
```

# Operation Specifications
TreeBuildingStrategy::getLastLevel
Summary:
Returns the final component of a level sequence.
Algorithm:
1. If levelSeq is null or empty, return 0.
2. Return the integer represented by the final EIntegerObject.
Related Features:
Integer level normalization and ROOT handling.
Related Classes:
EIntegerObject
Input:
levelSeq is a list of EIntegerObject values and may be empty.
Output:
An integer level value, or 0 for null, empty, or a missing final element.
Pre-condition:
Values in the sequence are valid integer representations.
Post-condition:
The sequence is not modified.

TreeBuildingStrategy::isRoot
Summary:
Determines whether a base node represents the synthetic root.
Algorithm:
1. If node is null, return false.
2. Return true if node.levelSeq is null or empty.
3. Return false if node.levelSeq is non-empty.
Related Features:
ROOT structural representation and title "ROOT".
Related Classes:
BaseNode
Input:
node is a BaseNode reference that may be null.
Output:
true for a node with no structural level sequence; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
node.levelSeq is readable when node is non-null.
Post-condition:
The node is not modified.

TreeBuildingStrategy::getPrefix
Summary:
Returns all but the final component of a level sequence.
Algorithm:
1. If levelSeq is null, return an empty list.
2. If levelSeq has zero or one element, return a new empty list.
3. Otherwise return a new list containing every element before the final
   element.
Related Features:
Prefix relationships used to find tree ancestors.
Related Classes:
EIntegerObject
Input:
levelSeq is a list of EIntegerObject values; it may be empty or contain one
value.
Output:
A new mutable list containing the level-sequence prefix, or an empty list.
Pre-condition:
Every supplied element is non-null.
Post-condition:
The original list is not changed, and modifying the returned list does not
affect it.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
TreeBuildingStrategy::getLastLevel
Summary:
Returns the final component of a level sequence.
Algorithm:
1. If levelSeq is null or empty, return 0.
2. Return the integer represented by the final EIntegerObject.
Related Features:
Integer level normalization and ROOT handling.
Related Classes:
EIntegerObject
Input:
levelSeq is a list of EIntegerObject values and may be empty.
Output:
An integer level value, or 0 for null, empty, or a missing final element.
Pre-condition:
Values in the sequence are valid integer representations.
Post-condition:
The sequence is not modified.

TreeBuildingStrategy::isRoot
Summary:
Determines whether a base node represents the synthetic root.
Algorithm:
1. If node is null, return false.
2. Return true if node.levelSeq is null or empty.
3. Return false if node.levelSeq is non-empty.
Related Features:
ROOT structural representation and title "ROOT".
Related Classes:
BaseNode
Input:
node is a BaseNode reference that may be null.
Output:
true for a node with no structural level sequence; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
node.levelSeq is readable when node is non-null.
Post-condition:
The node is not modified.

TreeBuildingStrategy::getPrefix
Summary:
Returns all but the final component of a level sequence.
Algorithm:
1. If levelSeq is null, return an empty list.
2. If levelSeq has zero or one element, return a new empty list.
3. Otherwise return a new list containing every element before the final
   element.
Related Features:
Prefix relationships used to find tree ancestors.
Related Classes:
EIntegerObject
Input:
levelSeq is a list of EIntegerObject values; it may be empty or contain one
value.
Output:
A new mutable list containing the level-sequence prefix, or an empty list.
Pre-condition:
Every supplied element is non-null.
Post-condition:
The original list is not changed, and modifying the returned list does not
affect it.

# Operation Specifications
StrictStrategy::isChild
Summary:
Tests whether one integer level sequence structurally extends another.
Algorithm:
1. Return false if parentSeq or childSeq is null.
2. Return false if childSeq.size() is not parentSeq.size() + 1.
3. For every index in parentSeq, require childSeq.get(i).equals(parentSeq.get(i)).
4. Return true if all prefix values match and one additional valid level
   value is present.
Related Features:
Ordered level semantics and the empty ROOT sequence.
Related Classes:
EIntegerObject
Input:
parentSeq and childSeq are lists of EIntegerObject values. parentSeq may be
empty for ROOT; childSeq must be non-null.
Output:
true if childSeq is exactly parentSeq followed by one valid level; otherwise
false.
Pre-condition:
Each list contains non-null, comparable EIntegerObject values.
Post-condition:
Neither list is modified.

StrictStrategy::buildTree
Summary:
Builds a document outline tree using strict parent-child level validation.
Algorithm:
1. If chain is null or empty, create and return a ROOT TreeNode.
2. Create ROOT with an empty level sequence.
3. Set the active current node to ROOT.
4. For each ChainNode in order:
   a. Reject it if its level sequence is empty while the current node is
     not ROOT, or if it does not satisfy isChild(currentSeq, nodeSeq).
   b. Otherwise create a TreeNode and attach it to the current node.
   c. Set current to the new node.
5. Return ROOT.
Related Features:
Empty ROOT sequence, strict level extension, sibling ordering, and
consistent parent links.
Related Classes:
ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy, BaseNode
Input:
chain is an ordered list of non-null ChainNodes. Its first node must have a
non-empty child level sequence; every later sequence must extend its direct
predecessor's sequence.
Output:
A TreeNode titled "ROOT" containing all validly attachable headings.
Pre-condition:
Every non-root ChainNode.levelSeq is non-null and begins with a non-empty
parent level sequence.
Post-condition:
Every child extends its parent's level sequence, all attached nodes are
reachable from ROOT, child order is preserved, and invalid chain data causes
a rejection before attachment.

StrictStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary:
Creates a detached TreeNode representation of a ChainNode for strict tree
construction.
Algorithm:
1. Allocate a TreeNode.
2. Copy the ChainNode's title, level sequence, level text, and content.
3. Initialize parent to null and children to an empty list.
4. Return the TreeNode.
Related Features:
TreeNode.parent, TreeNode.children, and inherited BaseNode fields.
Related Classes:
ChainNode, TreeNode, BaseNode
Input:
chainnode is a non-null ChainNode with initialized fields.
Output:
A detached TreeNode containing the ChainNode's document data.
Pre-condition:
chainnode is non-null.
Post-condition:
The returned TreeNode has no parent, has no children, and has copied heading
data and content.

# Operation Specifications
StrictStrategy::isChild
Summary:
Tests whether one integer level sequence structurally extends another.
Algorithm:
1. Return false if parentSeq or childSeq is null.
2. Return false if childSeq.size() is not parentSeq.size() + 1.
3. For every index in parentSeq, require childSeq.get(i).equals(parentSeq.get(i)).
4. Return true if all prefix values match and one additional valid level
   value is present.
Related Features:
Ordered level semantics and the empty ROOT sequence.
Related Classes:
EIntegerObject
Input:
parentSeq and childSeq are lists of EIntegerObject values. parentSeq may be
empty for ROOT; childSeq must be non-null.
Output:
true if childSeq is exactly parentSeq followed by one valid level; otherwise
false.
Pre-condition:
Each list contains non-null, comparable EIntegerObject values.
Post-condition:
Neither list is modified.

StrictStrategy::buildTree
Summary:
Builds a document outline tree using strict parent-child level validation.
Algorithm:
1. If chain is null or empty, create and return a ROOT TreeNode.
2. Create ROOT with an empty level sequence.
3. Set the active current node to ROOT.
4. For each ChainNode in order:
   a. Reject it if its level sequence is empty while the current node is
     not ROOT, or if it does not satisfy isChild(currentSeq, nodeSeq).
   b. Otherwise create a TreeNode and attach it to the current node.
   c. Set current to the new node.
5. Return ROOT.
Related Features:
Empty ROOT sequence, strict level extension, sibling ordering, and
consistent parent links.
Related Classes:
ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy, BaseNode
Input:
chain is an ordered list of non-null ChainNodes. Its first node must have a
non-empty child level sequence; every later sequence must extend its direct
predecessor's sequence.
Output:
A TreeNode titled "ROOT" containing all validly attachable headings.
Pre-condition:
Every non-root ChainNode.levelSeq is non-null and begins with a non-empty
parent level sequence.
Post-condition:
Every child extends its parent's level sequence, all attached nodes are
reachable from ROOT, child order is preserved, and invalid chain data causes
a rejection before attachment.

StrictStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary:
Creates a detached TreeNode representation of a ChainNode for strict tree
construction.
Algorithm:
1. Allocate a TreeNode.
2. Copy the ChainNode's title, level sequence, level text, and content.
3. Initialize parent to null and children to an empty list.
4. Return the TreeNode.
Related Features:
TreeNode.parent, TreeNode.children, and inherited BaseNode fields.
Related Classes:
ChainNode, TreeNode, BaseNode
Input:
chainnode is a non-null ChainNode with initialized fields.
Output:
A detached TreeNode containing the ChainNode's document data.
Pre-condition:
chainnode is non-null.
Post-condition:
The returned TreeNode has no parent, has no children, and has copied heading
data and content.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
TreeBuilder::buildTree
Summary:
Delegates construction of a ChainNode list to the configured tree-building
strategy and returns the resulting outline tree.
Algorithm:
1. If strategy is null, use a strict default implementation.
2. If chain is null, pass an empty list to strategy.buildTree.
3. Otherwise pass the supplied list unchanged.
4. Return strategy.buildTree(chain).
5. If the selected strategy throws for malformed structural data, propagate
   that exception without attaching the rejected node.
Related Features:
strategy polymorphism and ROOT fallback.
Related Classes:
TreeBuildingStrategy, ChainNode, TreeNode, StrictStrategy
Input:
chain is an ordered list of ChainNodes and may be null to represent no input.
Output:
The TreeNode returned by the selected strategy, normally titled "ROOT".
Pre-condition:
strategy is non-null, or a strict default is available.
Post-condition:
The selected strategy's tree invariants hold; the supplied chain is not
mutated.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
TreeExporter::exportTree
Summary:
Exports a tree using a deterministic text-outline format.
Algorithm:
1. If tree is null, reject the operation.
2. Initialize an empty result and invoke exportTreeInternal for ROOT.
3. Return the resulting plain-text representation.
Related Features:
Hierarchical traversal, one-line-per-node output, and title preservation.
Related Classes:
TreeNode, BaseNode
Input:
tree is a non-null TreeNode that is the root of the outline.
Output:
A string representing the tree through the tree-export format.
Pre-condition:
The tree has a ROOT node with an empty level sequence, and parent links are
consistent.
Post-condition:
No tree field is modified; equal trees with the same ordered structure produce
equal output.

TreeExporter::exportTreeInternal
Summary:
Recursively emits one formatted export line for a node and its descendants.
Algorithm:
1. Emit the node's level sequence followed by ": " and its title, terminating
   the line with a newline.
2. Iterate children in stored order.
3. For every child, invoke exportTreeInternal recursively with the required
   prefix, isLast, and isRoot state.
4. Apply connector and indentation characters according to the established
   outline format; if no connector format is defined, use a child offset of
   four spaces while preserving child order.
5. Return the accumulated representation.
Related Features:
Recursive parent-child traversal, stable indentation, and child order.
Related Classes:
TreeNode, BaseNode
Input:
node is the TreeNode to export.
prefix is the indentation or connector text already emitted for the path.
isLast states whether node is the last child of its parent.
isRoot states whether the current call represents the synthetic root.
Output:
A string containing the current node and all descendants, one node per line.
Pre-condition:
node is non-null, prefix is valid for the current path, and child lists are
ordered.
Post-condition:
Neither node nor its children are modified, and every reachable node appears
exactly once.

TreeExporter::exportToJsonFile
Summary:
Serializes a tree as formatted JSON and writes it to a specified filesystem
path.
Algorithm:
1. If tree is null, reject the operation.
2. If filePath is null, reject the operation.
3. Serialize the tree with exportToJson.
4. If the platform requires platform-specific encoding, encode the result as
   UTF-8 by default.
5. Create or truncate the file represented by filePath and write the JSON.
6. Flush and close the stream.
Related Features:
Deterministic child order and four-space JSON indentation.
Related Classes:
TreeNode, BaseNode, java.nio.file.Path
Input:
tree is a non-null rooted TreeNode.
filePath is a non-null Path identifying the destination.
Output:
No return value. A UTF-8 text file is created or replaced.
Pre-condition:
filePath identifies a writable location, and parent directories exist.
Post-condition:
The file contains the exported JSON and no longer reflects the tree as it
existed before any subsequent tree mutation.

TreeExporter::nodeToDict
Summary:
Projects one tree node into the map used by JSON serialization.
Algorithm:
1. Create an EMap.
2. Insert title, level_seq, level_text, content, and children keys.
3. Recursively project each child in child order.
4. Return the completed map.
Related Features:
JSON field names, nested children, and parent-derived structure.
Related Classes:
TreeNode, BaseNode, EMap
Input:
node is a non-null TreeNode.
Output:
An EMap with title, level_seq, level_text, content, and children entries.
Pre-condition:
node's BaseNode fields are initialized and its child list is non-null.
Post-condition:
A fresh map is returned and the input node is not modified.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

```java
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
```
```java
   * Parses structured text into an ordered list of heading and content ChainNodes
   * and always returns a synthetic ROOT section.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. Split text into lines using newline and recognize carriage returns as line
   *    boundaries.
   * 2. Initialize the result with a ChainNode titled "ROOT" and an empty level
   *    sequence.
   * 3. Maintain a current content string, initially empty.
   * 4. For each line in order:
   *    a. Call detectLevel.
   *    b. If it returns a heading node, append the accumulated ordinary text to
   *      the new heading as its initial content, append the node, and reset the
   *      accumulation.
   *    c. Otherwise, if the line is empty, append a newline to content so an
   *      empty line is still represented in the section text.
   *    d. Otherwise, append a newline between noncontiguous ordinary lines and
   *      then append the current line.
   * 5. Append any remaining ordinary text to the last chain node's content.
   * 6. Return the list containing ROOT first.
   * Related Features:
   * Pattern priority, first valid match, ordinary-text preservation, and synthetic
   * ROOT fallback.
   * Related Classes:
   * ChainParser, ChainNode, LevelPattern, ParserHelper
   * Input:
   * text is structured plain text. It may be null, empty, contain only
   * whitespace, or include mixed headings and content separated by \n or \r.
   * Each line's encoding is passed to detectLevel.
   * Output:
   * A non-null List<ChainNode>. The first node is titled "ROOT" with an empty
   * level sequence; later nodes preserve source order and have content.
   * Pre-condition:
   * patterns and ParserHelper are configured, and text is supplied in a Java
   * String whose characters are valid for the configured regexes.
   * Post-condition:
   * All source content is assigned to a section, headings retain source order,
   * only valid numeric patterns produce level sequences, and the result is never
```

   * @generated NOT

  public EList<ChainNode> parseToChain(final String text)
  {
    EList<ChainNode> result = new BasicEList<ChainNode>();
    ChainNode root = ArborparserFactory.eINSTANCE.createChainNode();
    root.setTitle("ROOT");
    result.add(root);

    if (text == null || text.isEmpty())
    {
      return result;
    }

    String[] lines = text.split("\\r?\\n", -1);
    StringBuilder content = new StringBuilder();
    ChainNode lastNode = root;

    for (String line : lines)
    {
      ChainNode heading = detectLevel(line);
      if (heading != null)
      {
        if (content.length() > 0)
        {
          heading.setContent(content.toString());
          content.setLength(0);
        }
        result.add(heading);
        lastNode = heading;
      }
      else if (line.isEmpty())
      {
        content.append('\n');
      }
      else
      {
        if (content.length() > 0 && content.charAt(content.length() - 1) != '\n')
        {
          content.append('\n');
        }
        content.append(line);
        lastNode.setContent(content.toString());
        content.setLength(0);
      }
    }

    if (content.length() > 0)
    {
      lastNode.setContent(content.toString());
    }

    return result;
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   * Finds the first valid heading pattern matching a line and creates a ChainNode
   * for the matched heading.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. If line is null, return null.
   * 2. Iterate patterns in their configured priority order.
   * 3. For each pattern, obtain its compiled regex through getRegex and attempt
   *    a match against line.
   * 4. Extract the matched numbering and title portions.
   * 5. Convert the matched numbering through LevelPattern.convertMatchedText.
   * 6. If conversion fails or produces no level sequence, continue to the next
   *    pattern.
   * 7. If multiple patterns match, retain the first pattern in the ordered list
   *    and call createChainNode with that pattern's priority.
   * 8. If no pattern converts successfully, return null.
   * Related Features:
   * ordered LevelPattern list, regex matching, number conversion, fixed level
   * sequence, level bounds, and first-match precedence.
   * Related Classes:
   * LevelPattern, ParserHelper, ChainNode, NumberType, EIntegerObject
   * Input:
   * line is a single non-null source-text line. The parser recognizes ordered
   * indicators, such as Arabic or Roman numbers, Chinese numerals, alphabetic
   * letters, and circled numbers, followed by a heading title.
   * Output:
   * A ChainNode for the first valid pattern, or null when line is empty,
   * unmatched, or has invalid numeric text.
   * Pre-condition:
   * patterns is non-null, contains valid patterns in priority order, and any
   * external ParserHelper is configured for the selected NumberType.
   * Post-condition:
   * The original line is not modified. On success, levelText contains matched
   * indicator text, title is the remaining heading text, and patternPriority
   * identifies the first valid pattern.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public ChainNode detectLevel(final String line)
  {
    if (line == null)
    {
      return null;
    }

    EList<LevelPattern> patternsList = getPatterns();
    if (patternsList == null)
    {
      return null;
    }

    int priority = 0;
    for (LevelPattern pattern : patternsList)
    {
      java.util.regex.Matcher matcher = pattern.getRegex().matcher(line);
      if (matcher.find())
      {
        String matchedText = matcher.group(1);
        String title = matcher.groupCount() >= 2 ? matcher.group(2) : "";
        if (title == null)
        {
          title = "";
        }

        EList<Integer> levelSeq = pattern.convertMatchedText(matchedText);
        if (levelSeq == null || levelSeq.isEmpty())
        {
          priority++;
          continue;
        }

        return createChainNode(levelSeq, title, "", matchedText, priority);
      }
      priority++;
    }
    return null;
  }

   * 1. Split text into lines using newline and recognize carriage returns as line
   *    boundaries.
   * 2. Initialize the result with a ChainNode titled "ROOT" and an empty level
   *    sequence.
   * 3. Maintain a current content string, initially empty.
   * 4. For each line in order:

   *    b. If it returns a heading node, append the accumulated ordinary text to
   *      the new heading as its initial content, append the node, and reset the

   *    c. Otherwise, if the line is empty, append a newline to content so an

   *    d. Otherwise, append a newline between noncontiguous ordinary lines and

   * whitespace, or include mixed headings and content separated by \n or \r.
   * Each line's encoding is passed to detectLevel.
   * Output:

   * level sequence; later nodes preserve source order and have content.

   * Post-condition:
   * All source content is assigned to a section, headings retain source order,
   * only valid numeric patterns produce level sequences, and the result is never

  public EList<ChainNode> parseToChain(final String text)
  {
    EList<ChainNode> result = new BasicEList<ChainNode>();
    ChainNode root = ArborparserFactory.eINSTANCE.createChainNode();
    root.setTitle("ROOT");
    result.add(root);

    if (text == null || text.isEmpty())
    {
      return result;
    }

    String[] lines = text.split("\\r?\\n", -1);
    StringBuilder content = new StringBuilder();
    ChainNode lastNode = root;

    for (String line : lines)
    {
      ChainNode heading = detectLevel(line);
      if (heading != null)
      {
        if (content.length() > 0)
        {
          heading.setContent(content.toString());
          content.setLength(0);
        }
        result.add(heading);
        lastNode = heading;
      }
      else if (line.isEmpty())
      {
        content.append('\n');
      }
      else
      {
        if (content.length() > 0)
        {
          content.append('\n');
        }
        content.append(line);
      }
    }

    if (content.length() > 0)
    {
      lastNode.setContent(content.toString());
    }

    return result;
  }

  public ChainNode detectLevel(final String line)
  {

    {
      return null;
    }

    EList<LevelPattern> patternsList = getPatterns();
    if (patternsList == null)
    {
      return null;
    }

    int priority = 0;
    for (LevelPattern pattern : patternsList)
    {
      java.util.regex.Matcher matcher = pattern.getRegex().matcher(line);
      if (matcher.find())
      {
        String matchedText = matcher.groupCount() >= 1 ? matcher.group(1) : matcher.group();
        String title = matcher.groupCount() >= 2 ? matcher.group(2) : "";
        if (title == null)
        {
          title = "";
        }
        if (matchedText == null)
        {
          matchedText = "";
        }

        EList<Integer> levelSeq = pattern.convertMatchedText(matchedText);
        if (levelSeq == null || levelSeq.isEmpty())
        {
          priority++;
          continue;
        }

        return createChainNode(levelSeq, title, "", matchedText, priority);
      }
      priority++;
    }
    return null;
  }

- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.
